title: Your First Weekend at Moravian University, Shared as Cards
description: A low-pressure, under-21-safe sequence that starts on North Campus and finishes with walkable Bethlehem history.

cards.title: 1. Get oriented on the Quad
cards.subtitle: Main Street Campus · first daylight stop
cards.notes: Start with a slow lap through the Quad, then use the surrounding buildings as landmarks before choosing a study or student-life stop.
cards.short_summary: A simple first look at the center of everyday North Campus activity.
cards.evidence_claim: Moravian identifies the Quad on North Campus as a place where students spend time, attend events, and participate in clubs and activities.
cards.access_notes: Located on Moravian’s Main Street (North) Campus; use the campus map to orient yourself.

cards.title: 2. Choose a study corner at Reeves
cards.subtitle: Main Street Campus · reset with your class materials
cards.notes: Bring a syllabus or reading list and test a study setup that fits you: carrel, group area, lounge seating, or a glass study room.
cards.short_summary: A practical early stop for learning the campus’s main study resource.
cards.evidence_claim: Reeves Library provides study space for more than 400 students, including glass study rooms, carrels, group areas, and lounge seating.
cards.access_notes: Library access and service availability can vary; check the library’s current hours before going.

cards.title: 3. Find the New Media Center
cards.subtitle: Reeves Library · make a note for future projects
cards.notes: Locate the New Media Center while you are already in Reeves so you know where to ask about audio or video work later in the term.
cards.short_summary: A quick reconnaissance stop for students who may need media-production space.
cards.evidence_claim: Moravian states that Reeves Library houses the Zinczenko New Media Center, including a video and audio recording studio.
cards.access_notes: Confirm equipment access, reservations, and staff availability with Reeves Library.

cards.title: 4. Learn the HUB layout
cards.subtitle: 1119 Monocacy Street · student-life hub
cards.notes: Walk through the HUB and save the information desk, Student Life suite, dining areas, and organization spaces as useful landmarks for the semester.
cards.short_summary: A central stop for finding services and campus connection points.
cards.evidence_claim: Moravian describes the HUB as a central gathering space that regularly hosts events, meetings, and programs and contains student services and dining.
cards.source_title: New Student Guide to Campus Life | Moravian University
cards.access_notes: The HUB is at 1119 Monocacy Street; specific offices and services may have separate availability.

cards.title: 5. Have a meal at the Star
cards.subtitle: HUB · plan around your dining access
cards.notes: Use a meal break to notice the HUB dining flow, then check the posted options and ask dining staff about navigating any dietary needs.
cards.short_summary: A campus meal stop integrated into the HUB rather than a separate trip.
cards.evidence_claim: Moravian identifies the Star, located in the HUB, as its largest dining room and includes it among new-student dining options.
cards.access_notes: Dining availability and payment options depend on current dining operations and your plan or account.

cards.title: 6. Check out the Doghouse
cards.subtitle: Moravian campus · weekday community space
cards.notes: On a weekday, bring your ID and use a short visit to see whether this community space could work for studying, relaxing, or meeting classmates.
cards.short_summary: A low-key campus space intended for current Moravian community members.
cards.evidence_claim: Moravian’s event policies describe the Doghouse as a community programming space accessible to current students on weekdays from 8 a.m. to 6 p.m. with an active ID.
cards.access_notes: Current Moravian students need an active University ID for weekday entry; the published access window is Monday–Friday, 8 a.m.–6 p.m.

cards.title: 7. Find Borhek Chapel
cards.subtitle: Comenius Hall · note it for campus programs
cards.notes: Locate the chapel from the north end of Comenius Hall and check campus communications for any public program that matches your interest.
cards.short_summary: A historic campus venue used for an array of University-sponsored programs.
cards.evidence_claim: Moravian says Borhek Chapel is at the north end of Comenius Hall and may be used during the academic year by University organizations.
cards.access_notes: The chapel is reservable; access depends on the scheduled program or organizer.

cards.title: 8. Add South Campus to your map
cards.subtitle: Priscilla Payne Hurd Campus · music and art area
cards.notes: Walk or travel to South Campus in daylight, find Foy Concert Hall, and keep it in mind when scanning future music and arts announcements.
cards.short_summary: A named performance venue on Moravian’s historic South Campus.
cards.evidence_claim: Moravian identifies the Priscilla Payne Hurd Campus as home to its music and art departments and lists Foy Concert Hall there.
cards.access_notes: Concert-hall entry depends on scheduled events or reservations; check the event listing before returning for a performance.

cards.title: 9. Browse the Moravian Book Shop
cards.subtitle: 428 Main Street · Historic Downtown Bethlehem
cards.notes: Take a daylight stroll to Main Street, browse the student bookstore section, and use the posted hours to plan a return if you need course supplies.
cards.short_summary: A downtown bookstore that also serves as Moravian University’s student bookstore.
cards.evidence_claim: Historic Bethlehem identifies the Moravian Book Shop at 428 Main Street as home to the Moravian University student bookstore.
cards.source_title: Moravian Book Shop | Visit Historic Bethlehem
cards.access_notes: The source lists daily public retail hours; purchases are optional.

cards.title: 10. End at the Colonial Industrial Quarter
cards.subtitle: 145 Ohio Road · outdoor historic grounds
cards.notes: Finish with a daylight walk through the grounds and along the creek; treat building interiors and any ticketed programming as separate plans.
cards.short_summary: An outdoor historic-site walk near downtown Bethlehem and the Monocacy Creek.
cards.evidence_claim: Historic Bethlehem states that the Colonial Industrial Quarter grounds at 145 Ohio Road are open daily from dawn to dusk.
cards.source_title: Colonial Industrial Quarter | Historic Bethlehem Museums & Sites
cards.access_notes: The grounds are open dawn to dusk; consult the site for specific building hours and ticketed-program details.
